scope: REQ-002 revision 1 AC-1 and AC-2, executed using VER-002 revision 1. Directed managed-record endpoint permissions and identity persistence; no broader core-conformance, standards-conformity or human-validation claim.

requirement.acceptance: AC-1: Create a permitted directed link and preserve its identity. AC-2: Reject disallowed endpoints; distinguish unrestricted endpoints from an explicitly empty allowed set.

methods: Create a need→component link using a named permitted relationship; update annotations without replacing UUID/endpoints.
Close/reopen SQLite and compare complete export, schema definitions and saved link. Forward query returns the link; reverse query does not.
Author the relationship in the production Model page, save a permitted connection through shared authoring and reload its exact native UUID/endpoints at 1440px/390px.
Exercise all 63 managed endpoint pairs across seven families: 16 permitted and 47 rejected. Cover directed, omitted/unrestricted, one-sided, empty source, empty target and both-empty constraints.
Two resource-only endpoint attempts remain rejected without explicit capability permissions; this is an adjacent guard, not a full REQ-027 re-audit.

Invalid relationship endpoint edits and model constraints, forbidden managed-type reclassification, undeclared endpoint types, missing endpoints and a mixed valid/invalid batch leave the complete recorded export unchanged.

Production authoring excludes restricted relationships for incompatible targets and reversed endpoints; Any remains available while empty-set families do not. A server-rejected target restriction retains the draft and exact saved project.

verificationHistory: The first UI attempt assumed title capitalization; changed to assert the selected native relationship value and option count.

An early reload occurred after native persistence but before UI confirmation; the existing uncertain-save lock correctly blocked model editing. The test now waits for the connection form to close after confirmed save. Both focused journeys then passed before the final full run.

limits: No runtime change was required; this audit adds criterion evidence and regressions for existing behavior.
The matrix covers configured managed types; explicit resource permissions and reference qualification have their own prior verification.
Managed types cannot be arbitrarily changed through ordinary entity edit; rejection of that attempt must not be read as type-migration support.
Stable relationship identity is tested through annotations and reopen. Endpoint direction is stored direction, independent of workflow display order.
Technical checks and primary-agent screenshot inspection do not establish representative-user validation.
Working tree includes earlier uncommitted work. Exact hashes identify assessed bytes, not a clean commit.
Older claims, snapshots and immutable evidence remain historical; observing edited supporting documents can reveal drift without rewriting outcomes.
